payload.title: proactive_priority._calibration_degraded reads the last row of judge-calibration.jsonl, which the judge_replay phase appends after the organic row every cycle, so the degraded_judges flag is read from the replay score and the organic degraded signal never raises opportunity
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/judge_calibration.py:703-711 (compute_judge_calibration appends one row per call, tagged with judgment_group_prefix)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/judge_calibration.py:681-685 (the docstring directs consumers to score_judges: the ledger tail is audit history, not a freshness source)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/cycle.py:2400-2411 (the judge_calibration phase appends the organic row)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/cycle.py:2363 (the judge_replay phase calls compute_replay_recall every cycle, appending a replay: row through the same writer)
payload.rule_violated: ORPHAN-HIGH-784 as stated in judge_calibration.py:681-685: the ledger tail is not a freshness source; one reader must not take a different population than the one its name asks about.
payload.notes: In every writable cycle the ledger's last row is the replay row (judgment_group_prefix 'replay:'), scored over gold-set groups only; with no active goldset it has no judge to degrade and degraded_judges is empty, so _calibration_degraded is False for every tool and the 0.1 opportunity for calibration_degraded is never added, whatever the organic scoring found. Close condition: Read the organic report only (the last row whose judgment_group_prefix is None) or call score_judges as the docstring directs. Test: append an organic row with degraded_judges ['j'] followed by a replay row with none, and assert compute_proactive_priorities adds calibration_degraded (red today). Verified at origin/main d716541239.
